paragraphs: North West England is a region made up of many councils, from Cumbria and Lancashire down through Merseyside and Cheshire to Greater Manchester, each with its own fostering service, alongside the independent agencies shown above. Our North West page describes the recruitment hubs in Lancashire and Cumbria and in Cheshire and Merseyside; this page adds Greater Manchester, home to the largest group of councils in the region.

All ten Greater Manchester councils recruit together as Foster for Greater Manchester. Anyone who enquires is promised a reply within one working day and a guide through each step, and every area offers local training, support groups and specialist social workers who match children with carers. To apply you need to be over 21, have your own home or a secure tenancy with room for a child, and good spoken and written English. In October 2023 the ten councils' lead members for children signed a Fostering Promise committing them to honest communication with carers and to respecting their professional role.

The city region says it has nearly 1,500 foster carers. Its Room Makers scheme followed a 2021 survey that found more than 100 carers had a room they could not yet use for fostering; the first round funded work that created 26 new bedrooms.

Every fostering service in the North West must pay at least the national minimum allowance for the rest of England, which for 2026-27 is £176 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £182 for 3 to 4, £201 for 5 to 10, £227 for 11 to 15 and £267 for 16 to 17. Many services add a fee for the carer. Look at the page for your own town, then speak to your council and to two or three of the agencies above.
